title: Two witnesses (Revelation 11)
hookLine: two prophets killed and raised; the kingdoms become the kingdom of our Lord

cards: Two bodies lie in the street of a great city. Nobody is allowed to bury them. People from every nation come to stare, and the mood is a party: neighbors trade gifts, glad these two are finally quiet.
They had been prophets in sackcloth, saying what the city didn't want to hear. Then, after three and a half days, something moves. Breath comes back into them.
They stand up on their feet, and the watchers are terrified. A voice from heaven calls: come up here. And the two witnesses rise into a cloud while their enemies watch.

teach.h: MOSES AND ELIJAH, OR THE CHURCH?
teach.b: Revelation eleven names them plainly: "my two witnesses." A witness says what they've seen, out loud, even when it costs them. First, who are they?

They can shut the sky so no rain falls, and turn water into blood. Some readers hear Elijah, who shut the rain, and Moses, who turned the Nile to blood. Others read the two as a picture of the whole witnessing church.

The text calls them "the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth," and leaves it there. Second, where they die: in the great city, "where also our Lord was crucified."

teach.h: THEY WALK THE ROAD HE WALKED.
teach.b: Their story walks his road: faithful words, a violent death, a watching crowd, and then "the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet." Third, the trumpet.

Soon after they rise, the seventh angel sounds, and loud voices in heaven say: "The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever."
Handel set very nearly those words in the Hallelujah chorus of his Messiah. Fourth, the street thought the story was over. The witnesses didn't win by shouting louder.
They kept saying what they'd seen.

teach.h: THE STREET'S PARTY ISN'T THE END.
teach.b: And when they stood, "great fear fell upon them which saw them," and the party went quiet.

how: Christians speak of bearing witness as telling, plainly and honestly, what they have seen of God, and choirs in churches and concert halls sing Revelation 11:15 in Handel's Hallelujah chorus.

games.q: you're in the great city. the two prophets who troubled everyone lie dead in the street. what does the crowd do?
o: leave them unburied, celebrate, and trade gifts.
go home quietly and say nothing.
games.why: the crowd refuses them a grave and throws a party. then breath comes back into them, they stand up, and the watchers are afraid.

practice: A witness isn't loud, just honest about what they've seen. Bring back one good thing you saw with your own eyes, a stranger's kindness, someone who forgave, a prayer that held you up, and hold the faces and the place clearly.
If you pray, ask for the chance and the courage to tell it simply; if not, just think of who might need to hear it.

wordCard.voice: Two witnesses. The prophets of Revelation eleven who speak, are killed, lie in the street, and stand up again when the Spirit of life enters them.

orig.note: Greek: a witness, someone who testifies to what they have seen.

carryVoice: Your line: he shall reign. Heaven's answer to a street that thought the story was over. Same time tomorrow.
